Client parity (R02, A33) follows one capability catalog ([ADR 0020](decisions/0020-capability-catalog-and-tui.md)): `schemas/capability-catalog.json` lists every product action with its runtime route, `@luuna/api-client` method, desktop control marker and TUI command; `scripts/check-contracts.mjs` validates it against the runtime's served routes and the typed client. The failure explanations (`packages/api-client/src/failures.ts`) are shared by the desktop and the terminal client `packages/tui` (`luuna-tui`, interactive menus and a scriptable non-interactive mode, SSE event following with resumption, hidden token entry, full-hash approval acknowledgment). Parity evidence: the TUI command test, the desktop marker test and `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs`. Actions still arriving from M4/M5/M7 join the catalog as they land.

The workspace should add crates when they contain a real contract or implementation: domain, storage, runtime/API, engine/Pi, Git, executor, validation, and external adapters. Shared frontend packages are created when an actual shared consumer needs them. Empty placeholders do not establish implementation progress.

## Runtime ownership

Only the Rust runtime may enforce state transitions, immutable plan hashes, approval scope, execution permissions, task dependencies, limits, retries, candidate identity, check evidence, review acceptance, and publication gates. Agents provide proposals and worker output. Deterministic runtime code produces authoritative domain events.

An approval binds to the complete canonical executable plan, its revision and hash, repository scope, base commits, check recipes, resource profiles, and budgets. Feature implementation requires a valid approval and a passing baseline. New code, rebases, dependency changes, and manual edits invalidate affected evidence. Review and publication refer to exact candidates; model text saying “passed” is never command evidence. The desktop displays the entire immutable plan and full hash and requires acknowledgment before enabling approval. Managed Git checkout, status, staging and commit disable configured clean, smudge and process filters with per-command overrides; these operations do not authorize repository-configured commands.

Native execution uses host permissions. Stronger isolation requires an explicitly configured execution profile with actual operating-system or container boundaries. Preserve developer changes and only clean up resources whose Luuna ownership is verified.

## Persistence and ticket authority

SQLite owns Luuna projects, immutable plan revisions, approvals, run/attempt lifecycle, sequenced events, check/review evidence, artifact references, and publication reconciliation. State mutation and emitted durable domain events must be committed consistently. Sensitive transcripts and provider data remain private artifacts with controlled access and retention.

The schema is versioned and append-only. At startup the runtime refuses a database that fails SQLite's quick check or was written by a newer schema, before writing anything to it. It applies only missing migrations, after an automatic pre-migration snapshot under `<data>/backups/`. `luuna-runtime backup` takes a consistent online snapshot. `luuna-runtime restore` needs the runtime stopped, verifies the snapshot, and moves the current database and its `-wal`/`-shm` aside before installing it. `luuna-runtime check` reports integrity and schema version. A snapshot covers the database only; artifacts and worktrees are files, so a complete backup is the data directory copied after an orderly stop. Startup recovery skips records it cannot decode, logs them by table and ID, and still settles their state where it can. See [ADR 0016](decisions/0016-storage-backup-and-schema-compatibility.md).

Baselines are runs: `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines` executes a repository's confirmed required recipes through the supervised executor and records `CheckResult` evidence bound to the manifest hash, exact commit and tree, and an environment fingerprint, with private hashed artifacts. `Implementing` is entered only through the transactional gate that re-checks the approval, the current manifest and a passed matching baseline per repository; see [ADR 0007](decisions/0007-baseline-executor.md). One baseline per repository runs at a time. Every check's process group is recorded; whatever a check leaves running is terminated before its result is recorded, and startup recovery terminates verified survivors of checks a hard-killed runtime left behind (Windows checks run in kill-on-close job objects). Missing tools or dependencies and checks cut short by the workflow budget are blocked infrastructure, never failures a repair is asked to fix (ADR 0007 amendment, 2026-10-21).

Projects are registered from existing repositories. The confirmed **project manifest** (`schemas/project.schema.json`, hashed with `luuna-json-v1`) is machine-independent and append-only by revision; the **machine registry** maps each repository ID to its local path and the identity observed at registration (the redacted configured remote plus the root commits reachable from HEAD). A later observation must show an equivalent remote and contain those roots; only an explicit, evented rebind changes a binding. A checkout is registered once and never overlaps the runtime data directory. Discovery proposals and project-scoped events (`project.registered`, `repository.registered`, `repository.rebound`, `discovery.proposed`, `manifest.confirmed`) are durable, and replaying the project stream reconstructs the confirmed map. Inspection never writes to a repository or executes its text, including filters configured in submodules; see [ADR 0006](decisions/0006-repository-import.md).

Discovery also probes the host once per proposal (`Discovery.host_capabilities`: each profile tool resolved on `PATH` and asked only for its version) and annotates every proposed check with `capability: available | missing` and its missing tools, raising a `missing-tool` question rather than dropping the recipe; a confirmed check whose tool is absent is recorded `blocked`, never `failed`. Every advertised profile (Node, React, Next.js, TypeScript, Go, Python, Rust, Flutter, native Android, native iOS) proposes real recipes; iOS and Android device recipes carry capabilities (`xcode`, `android-device`) this host cannot satisfy and say so. New projects are created only through a hashed `ScaffoldProposal` (`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold/propose`: files, baseline recipes, generator and network steps, tool probes, `ready | blocked`) that the developer confirms by exact hash (`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold`): the runtime writes the files, commits, runs the baseline recipe through the supervised executor as a real check, registers the project and records `project.scaffolded`; a failing baseline is returned as such and never reported passing. Android and iOS scaffolds are blocked proposals naming their platform generators. See [ADR 0019](decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md); capable-runner evidence for Go, Flutter, Android and iOS remains open.

Legacy projects retain the explicitly temporary SQLite ticket source until component activation. `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/components` durably initializes the private component workspace and migrates tickets while preserving IDs and numeric revisions. Enabled projects use Missions (Seeds-derived) as authority for ticket intent, acceptance criteria, status, dependencies and source fingerprints; SQLite stores its revision-aware projection and Luuna execution state. GET/list return the last reconciled projection; `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}/source` reports actual source freshness and `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/reconcile` requires the expected projection revision. External edits advance the reconciled revision and invalidate stale plans; freshness, ticket readiness and dependencies are rechecked at runtime work/evidence boundaries. Missing components fail closed. There are never two independently writable authorities for these fields. See [ADR 0003](decisions/0003-ticket-authority.md) and [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md).

## Pi and maintained components

Pi is the agent engine, not the scheduler or validation authority. The engine contract supervises process creation, assignments, followups, events, stop requests, inspection, and disposal. Use a tested pinned release, strict JSONL framing, command correlation, bounded buffers, timeouts, and owned child-process cleanup. Stderr is diagnostic data. Prompt acceptance and agent settlement are separate events. Persist attempts so interrupted processes cannot become successful runs after restart.

Luuna maintains three branded CLI distributions: **Missions** (`@luuna/missions-cli`, Seeds-derived), **Atlas** (`@luuna/atlas-cli`, Mulch-derived), and **Beacon** (`@luuna/beacon-cli`, Canopy-derived). They live under `components/missions`, `components/atlas`, and `components/beacon` as separate package and integration boundaries. Preserve compatible underlying APIs/data formats, upstream copyright and MIT notices. Prefer adapters over rewrites or direct SQLite access to their records.

The owner resumed extraction on October 21, 2026 and explicitly authorized public component repositories. Missions, Atlas and Beacon now live in `brodynelly/luuna-missions`, `brodynelly/luuna-atlas` and `brodynelly/luuna-beacon`; Luuna stays private and consumes exact-commit Git submodules at the existing components paths. The manifest and gitlinks bind dependency identity; setup uses frozen Bun locks without lifecycle scripts, and consumer smoke checks exercise real CLI/JSON operations. Each destination owns its CI and source; registry packages remain private and unpublished. See [ADR 0012](decisions/0012-independent-component-repositories.md), superseding ADR 0002's hosted-extraction deferral.

The runtime now invokes these pinned CLIs through `luuna-components` with bounded input/output, a fixed stdin bridge, isolated HOME/config, sanitized environment, source/toolchain verification and owned process cleanup. Explicit per-project activation uses `<data_dir>/components/projects/<id>`; explicit user memory uses `<data_dir>/components/user`. It never adopts developer or imported stores. Atlas memory exposes explicit scope and provenance; Beacon exposes versioned prompt preview/update. A user selects resources for a plan, whose canonical optional `component_context` contains their exact snapshots, identities and hashes. The runtime rejects changed selected sources at approval and execution/evidence boundaries and gives workers only approved bounded content. Durable intent ledgers reconcile uncertain component writes before retry. Imported development metadata is not runtime data or permission to load instructions into agents. See [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md) for activation, ticket reconciliation, resource selection and native-process limits. Memory promotion widens scope one step at a time (`process -> project -> user`) through `POST …/memory/{id}/promote` with the displayed hash, creating the wider record with provenance naming its origin and deleting the narrower one under the same intent ledger; `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/export` returns the manifest, ticket projections, project and process memory and current prompts, and is refused outright when it would carry user memory, a credential value or a path of this host ([ADR 0021](decisions/0021-memory-promotion-and-project-export.md)). Import of an export, retention policy and supported-platform evidence remain obligations.

## Candidate validation and review

Migration 5 stores exact candidate commit/tree identities, append-only validation generations and structured independent reviews. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` names the expected hash and optionally `auto_repair`; it executes the approved required recipes inside the owned candidate worktree and starts a fresh read-only Pi reviewer only after the checks pass. Checks and reviews cannot be reused across candidate revisions or interrupted generations. A `failed` candidate whose required checks all passed in its current generation and whose reviewer left no verdict (invalid or self-inconsistent output, a refused session) may re-enter validation in place as generation `n+1`: same revision, approval and budgets, fresh checks and a fresh reviewer, no writer attempt; `GET …/candidate` reports that decision as `revalidate_allowed`. `GET …/candidate` and `GET …/diff` expose authoritative evidence and exact diffs; `POST …/repair` rechecks current approval, baseline/host and remaining aggregate budgets before creating the next scoped candidate. Model output never supplies command evidence. Repair writers receive the previous candidate's reason, check records, review and a bounded tail of each failed check log, never the private artifact paths. See [ADR 0009](decisions/0009-candidate-validation-review.md).

Since the second 2026-10-21 amendment to ADR 0009, every validation generation starts from the candidate tree alone: the owned worktree is verified and its untracked and ignored paths are removed and recorded. Content drift fails the candidate with a reason naming the change and the next step and is never re-validated in place. Review diffs ignore attributes that hide changes and are bounded with every changed path listed; a non-passing review must name a finding; reviewer tool calls are recorded by tool and path. `GET …/candidate` reports `validate_allowed` and `decision_reasons` from the gates the routes apply.

Automatic repair is opt-in and bounded by both the immutable plan and project repair policy. Infrastructure errors stop without repeated edits. Interrupted check and review stages retain elapsed usage up to their last durable heartbeat; a reviewer interrupted after its durable prompt marker, and every interrupted writer, reserve unknown spend and require re-planning when headroom is exhausted. Clients see aggregate workflow usage against the plan budgets and cumulative per-ticket usage, including spend the provider reported without a price. Review success is evidence for an exact candidate only; publication and human-controlled merge remain separate gates.

## Multi-repository coordination

A plan may carry several tasks, each on a distinct registered repository, with `depends_on` naming the tasks that must complete first; the contract refuses self, unknown, duplicate and cyclic dependencies by name, and bounds `budgets.max_workers` to the task count and the runtime's four-run limit. Discovery proposes `package` relationships between registered repositories from `package.json` dependencies, `Cargo.toml` path dependencies and `go.mod` replace directives with evidence and `confirmed: false`; confirming a manifest that still lists an unconfirmed relationship is refused, and confirmed relationships must be acyclic. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` on such a plan runs the task graph: after the same gates as one writer (with one environment fingerprint per repository), tasks whose dependencies completed run concurrently up to `max_workers`, never two writers in one repository, each as a writer attempt in its own owned worktree, with every completed producer bound into the consumer's writer environment and prompt as `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_<REPOSITORY>_PATH`/`…_COMMIT`. Per-task state is durable (migration 10, `GET …/tasks`, `task.*` events); a dependency's failure blocks its dependents with the reason, cancellation records every task, a restart marks running tasks interrupted and keeps completed commits and worktrees, and `implement` with `task_id` resumes a failed, blocked or interrupted task under the original approval within the approved budgets (an attempt lost mid-prompt still reserves the remaining cost budget, so re-planning follows as for one writer). When every task completed, one candidate set freezes every repository's exact commit and the `<consumer>:<producer>` bindings; validation runs every repository's required recipes in its own candidate worktree with the same bindings, binds results to exact commits, fails the set naming the repository and recipe (`integration blocked`) when a consumer check fails, and gives the fresh reviewer one bounded combined diff. Repair of a multi-repository set is re-planning. See [ADR 0017](decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md); delegated roles (P42) and dependency overrides (P44) remain open.

## Publication and host diagnostics

A `reviewed` candidate with a `passed` review may be published (`POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publish` with the exact hash and an idempotency key) to GitHub only, by the repository's registered identity: the runtime pushes each repository's exact candidate commit to `luuna/<ticket>/<hash prefix>` and opens one pull request per repository against the manifest's default branch, linking them when there are several. Every external write is preceded by a durable intent (migration 11: `publications`, `publication_intents`) and looked up by its stable identity first (`git ls-remote` for the branch, the pull-request head for the PR), so a timeout after remote success, a partial publication and a replayed key never duplicate anything; `POST …/publication/reconcile` retries only steps the ledger does not show succeeded. `GET …/publication` refreshes CI (check runs and commit status) and merge observation under bounded timeouts; a failing CI is reported distinctly and changes no evidence, and `integrated` is set only when every pull request is observed merged by a person. There is no merge route or call; a test asserts it. The GitHub token (`LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN`) reaches Git only through scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*` headers and the REST client as a bearer header; only its presence is ever reported. Events: `publication.requested`, `publication.pushed`, `publication.pr_opened`, `publication.failed`, `publication.reconciled`, `publication.integrated`. `luuna-runtime doctor [--json]` reports Git, Python, Node, the pinned Pi probe, the data directory and database, token and credential presence by name, the service port and the component toolchain, exiting 1 when a required item is missing. See [ADR 0018](decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md); every publication test runs against a fake GitHub API and a local bare remote, so real GitHub evidence remains M7 exit work. `scripts/package-windows.ps1` builds an unsigned NSIS development installer carrying the desktop, the release runtime, the Windows helper scripts and the pinned Pi tree; the native bootstrap of ADR 0011 prefers that packaged layout when it is present beside the executable.

## API and service lifetime

All application routes use `/api/v1`. Implemented project routes are `POST /api/v1/projects` (register existing repositories by absolute root path), `GET /api/v1/projects[/{id}]`, `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/discover` (read-only proposal), `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/manifest` (confirm with `expected_revision`), `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/repositories/{repository_id}/rebind` (explicitly re-point a moved or re-identified checkout) and `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/events`. The canonical create-ticket route is **`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets`** (implemented in M2c with an idempotency key; enabled projects use the Missions authority of ADRs 0003/0014). Do not add a parallel `POST /api/v1/tickets` alias. Other operations address ticket, plan, and run identities: `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans` records the next immutable plan revision and opens its workflow run, `POST /api/v1/plans/{id}/approvals` approves one exact hash, `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` schedules the writer after transactional revalidation, and `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/worktrees` and `/attempts` expose the Luuna-owned worktree leases and attempts (ADR 0008). Commands that can create work require idempotency; operations sensitive to stale state require expected revisions. SSE streams use durable event IDs/cursors for replay and deduplication. Artifacts use authorized IDs, never arbitrary request-supplied filesystem paths.

Bind the development service to loopback and authenticate protected API actions. A development launch may use an explicitly managed foreground process. The desktop reconnects to that service; closing a window or losing SSE does not decide run lifetime. Explicit shutdown stops or reconciles owned workers and persists interruption: since 2026-10-21 work stopped by Ctrl+C or SIGTERM is recorded `interrupted` (resumable after restart), never `cancelled`, and the client shows a lost runtime as an outage, reconnects by itself and reloads authoritative state when the runtime answers again. A Tauri child/sidecar alone does not prove independent lifetime. Platform-specific startup, supervision, token storage, and shutdown must be tested before distribution. See [ADR 0004](decisions/0004-service-lifecycle.md).

## Milestone evidence

Windows orderly service stop is `POST /api/v1/shutdown`, authenticated with the
existing bearer token. The runtime closes scheduling admission, drains admitted
mutation handlers, interrupts owned work and exits cleanly; window closure is
still only a client disconnect. Windows scripts reuse the DPAPI-encrypted token
and data directory across restart. See [ADR 0010](decisions/0010-authenticated-service-shutdown.md).

The initial tool-free connectivity slice exposes authenticated run creation/history, cursor event replay and SSE, and cancellation. M2a adds read-only repository import, discovery proposals and confirmed manifest revisions; M2b adds supervised baselines with bound evidence; M2c adds temporary local tickets, immutable plan revisions, exact-hash approvals, Luuna-owned worktree leases and one scoped writer whose candidate waits in `validating`. M3 adds candidate-bound required checks, a fresh read-only reviewer, structured findings, optional bounded automatic repairs and conservative restart recovery; its genuine-provider exit is closed on Linux (see the status report) while native Mac/Windows lifecycle evidence remains open. The bounded M6 component slice adds explicit Missions migration/reconciliation and selected Atlas/Beacon plan resources. Publication, broader M6 parity and supported-platform exits remain separate capabilities.

| Milestone | Required proof | Does not establish completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0 | Locked build, schema fixtures, deterministic approval/transition rejection, durable state checks | Folder creation or documentation checks alone |
| M1 | Real pinned Pi/provider session, streamed API events, persistence, cancellation, error handling and restart evidence | Scripted worker or fixture-only protocol tests |
| M2a | Real and synthetic imports with byte-identical checkouts, rejected invalid/mismatched repositories, proposed (not executed) recipes, confirmed manifest replay after restart | A proposed manifest, a stored recipe, or any claim that a baseline ran |
| M2b | Genuine passing and failing baselines with commit/tree/environment-bound results and hashed artifacts; missing executable, empty suite, dirty checkout, deadline, cancellation and restart recorded as blocked/failed/cancelled/interrupted; stale baseline cannot enter implementation | A writer, a worktree, or any run that modifies a repository |
| M2c | One approved fixture feature changed only its Luuna-owned worktree with the developer checkout byte-identical; missing or stale approval, changed base, changed recipe, unrelated repository or path, stale baseline, second writer and exceeded budget refused; cancellation and restart preserve the worktree and void the attempt; a genuine pinned-Pi writer run through a real provider | Validation of the candidate, independent review, repair or any publication (M3+); any claim that prompt or guard scoping is an OS boundary |
| M3 | Candidate commit/tree/hash frozen; required checks executed in the owned worktree before any review; a fresh, separately identified read-only reviewer whose structured verdict the runtime enforces; a seeded failing check needing a new repair revision with fresh evidence; bounded automatic repair pausing at the attempt budget; cancellation and hard-kill recovery with reaped children and reserved spend; a genuine provider-backed run of all of the above (closed on Linux, October 17, 2026) | Fixture reviewer verdicts as provider evidence; a model's self-assessment as check evidence; native Mac/Windows lifecycle, which stays open; any publication or merge |
| Desktop integration | Real service connection, run actions, streamed state and reconnection | Frontend build or decorative simulation alone |
| Full v1 | Original requirements/acceptance matrix including browser/TUI parity and supported platform evidence | Single-repository Linux demo |

Required foundation checks are schema validation, Rust formatting/tests/lint, frontend type/build checks, and relevant fixture integration tests. Native desktop compilation requires platform prerequisites. Real provider smoke tests require existing credentials/model access and are reported separately. Mac/Windows jobs provide compatibility evidence only when they have actually run.

Luuna's original code and documentation are MIT licensed. Derived component distributions retain separate upstream notices. The original `VALIDATION-REPORT.md` validates a documentation delivery; keep product evidence separate. Registry package publication, signed installers, remote access, and production release still require explicit operational decisions and evidence; [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) is the M8 report that links every requirement and acceptance scenario to what has actually run and names what blocks the v1 label.

PR 11 preservation follow-up: historical artifact filenames remain readable;
identity-changing rebinds withdraw manifest confirmation without deleting history;
new plan revisions cannot bypass live-work guards. These guards are transactional
runtime policy. The desktop exposes cumulative ticket usage and diff omissions.
An interrupted restore resumes its durable intent before SQLite can open or create
the main file, keeping original database files and sidecars together in backups.


---

Source: /docs/docs-design-system

# Luuna desktop design system

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: current; decision recorded in [ADR 0013](decisions/0013-desktop-design-system.md). This is the visual and interaction contract for the desktop client (`apps/desktop`). It is presentation only: the runtime decides every state, permission, reason and next step, and the client displays them. A design change may never change which control appears, when it is enabled, or what text the runtime's state produces.

## Principles

1. **Green is earned.** The success tone means passed durable evidence: a passed check or baseline, a reviewed candidate or run, a `passed` review verdict, and a live authenticated connection. A completed demo session, an approval or a recorded candidate is not evidence and is never green. The UI's own copy says so: "A completed session is not a validation result."
2. **Six tones, three channels.** Every state is carried by a colour family, a shape mark and the unchanged runtime text. Colour is never the only signal, and no tone has two meanings.
3. **Identities are shown whole.** Hashes, commits, trees, fingerprints, sessions, worktree paths and artifact ids render in `code`: monospace, wrapping anywhere. CSS never truncates them. The only short forms are the leading-prefix slices that summary rows already make in code.
4. **Reason, then next step.** A recorded reason carries the tone of the state it explains. The next allowed step follows it on its own line, ruled in lavender.
5. **Interruption is not failure.** Outages, restarts, interrupted work and abandoned leases use the interrupted tone (plum, pause bars), never danger. Their work is durable.
6. **Lavender means the developer acts; cyan means the runtime works.** The brand lavender marks primary actions, the next step, focus and selection. The active tone is cyan, so runtime activity is never confused with a call to action. An action group has at most one primary button.
7. **Tokens only.** Literal colours, lengths and durations live in `design/tokens.css` alone. Every colour exists in the dark and the light scheme, and every text pair meets WCAG 2.1 AA.
8. **One page, one outline.** Heading levels follow the document outline in DOM order (h1, h2 per panel, h3 per subpanel, h4 inside a candidate). Visual order equals DOM order at every width.

## Files and layers

```text
apps/desktop/src/
  styles.css                 manifest: @layer tokens, base, components, screens; then @import … layer(…)
  design/tokens.css          the only file with literals; dark :root, light under prefers-color-scheme
  design/base.css            element defaults: type, code/pre, focus, forms, buttons
  design/components.css      tone indirection and every reusable component
  design/tone.ts             Tone type and exhaustive maps from runtime unions to tones
  design/StatusBadge.tsx     the one status chip
  design/design-system.test.ts   enforcement (run by npm test)
  screens/app.css            shell: topbar, intro, connection, workspace, history, events, footer
  screens/projects.css       Projects panel
  screens/workflows.css      tickets, plan controls, plan review
  screens/candidate-review.css   candidate evidence, checks, diff, verdict
  screens/project-components.css tickets, scoped memory and versioned prompts
```

Vite inlines the imports into one bundled stylesheet served from `'self'`, which the Tauri CSP allows. Later layers win regardless of specificity, so a screen rule refines a component without `!important`. No font, script or stylesheet is fetched.

## Tokens

Dark is the default; the light scheme redefines every colour under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)`. Values are hex so the contrast test computes ratios from the file itself.

| Role | Dark | Light | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-bg` | `#101216` | `#f5f6f9` | page |
| `--color-surface` | `#191d24` | `#ffffff` | panel |
| `--color-surface-raised` | `#20252e` | `#f8f9fb` | record row, tray, hover |
| `--color-surface-sunken` | `#0d1014` | `#eceff4` | pre, scroll regions |
| `--color-field` / `-disabled` | `#0d1014` / `#191d24` | `#ffffff` / `#eef1f5` | text fields: enabled well, disabled |
| `--color-control` / `-hover` | `#262c36` / `#353c47` | `#f6f7f9` / `#eceff3` | secondary button (disabled buttons are ghosted: no fill) |
| `--color-selected` / `-border` | `#262e40` / `#435579` | `#e8ecf8` / `#8f9fd6` | selected card |
| `--color-border` | `#303640` | `#d3d9e2` | decorative dividers |
| `--color-border-control` | `#6e788a` | `#7d8697` | control edges (3:1 non-text) |
| `--color-text` | `#e9edf4` | `#191d24` | body text |
| `--color-text-muted` | `#a7b0bf` | `#4a5363` | labels, terms, scope, small |
| `--color-text-subtle` | `#8f9aac` | `#5c6576` | meta: times, event numbers, placeholders |
| `--color-text-disabled` | `#7a8494` | `#7d8697` | disabled controls (exempt from 1.4.3) |
| `--color-accent` / `-hover` | `#b7c8fb` / `#d1dcff` | `#3b4fa0` / `#30418a` | primary, next step, links, selection |
| `--color-on-accent` | `#101216` | `#ffffff` | text on accent |
| `--color-focus` | `#c3d1ff` | `#3b4fa0` | focus ring |

Each tone has `--tone-<name>-fg` (text), `-bg` (tint), `-border` and `-mark` (shape) in both schemes; see `tokens.css`.

Scales: type `--text-2xs` 11 px (badges, eyebrow, meta), `--text-xs` 12 px (evidence, labels, code), `--text-sm` 13 px (controls, card text, h4), `--text-md` 14 px (body, h3), `--text-lg` 16 px (h2), `--text-xl` fluid 26 to 34 px (h1); weights 400, 550, 650; space on a 4 px rhythm (`--space-1` 4 px to `--space-7` 48 px, plus 2 px and 6 px half steps); radii 4, 7, 11 px; `--border-width` 1 px, `--rule-width` 3 px, `--focus-width` 2 px; controls and single-line fields 34 px (28 px small buttons); layout `--layout-max` 1280 px with a gutter of 40, 24 and 16 px at full width, 920 px and 680 px; textareas start at their `rows` with a 68 px floor; `--scroll-max` 28 rem and `--plan-max` 24 rem for bounded regions; one motion duration, `--duration-fast` 120 ms, which is 0 ms under reduced motion.

## Tones

| Tone | Meaning | Mark | Runtime values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| success (green) | passed durable evidence | filled circle | run `reviewed`; candidate `reviewed`; check and baseline `passed`; verdict `passed`; connection connected |
| active (cyan) | the runtime is working | ring | run `running`, `exploring`, `implementing`, `validating`, `reviewing`; candidate `validating`, `reviewing`; baseline `running`; lease `active` |
| danger (rose) | failed or blocked evidence | diamond | run `failed`, `testing_blocked`; candidate `failed`, `testing_blocked`; check and baseline `failed`, `blocked`; verdict `changes_required`, `blocked`; severity `blocking` |
| attention (amber) | waiting on the developer | triangle | run `plan_ready`, `approved`, `paused`; candidate `paused`; severity `warning`; recipe confidence `inferred`; project `unconfirmed` |
| neutral (slate) | recorded, not evidence | bar | run `queued`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `discovered`; candidate `pending`, `cancelled`; check `cancelled`; severity `info`; lease `released`; connection offline |
| interrupted (plum) | stopped by an outage or restart, recoverable | pause bars | `interrupted` everywhere; lease `abandoned`; connection reconnecting |

`design/tone.ts` holds these as `Record<Union, Tone>` maps over the `@luuna/api-client` unions, so a new runtime state fails `npm run typecheck` until it is given a tone. Descriptor chips (`manifest r2`, `ticket r1 · …`, `required · observed`) take no tone and render as outlined chips.

## Components

| Component | Markup | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status badge | `<StatusBadge tone={…}>{text}</StatusBadge>` renders `span.state[data-tone]` | Text is exactly the runtime value (underscores replaced as the screen already does); badges never transform case. Never add words inside the badge. |
| Tone mark | `i.tone-mark[data-tone]` (`aria-hidden`) | The badge's shape on its own, for a status dot outside a badge (the connection status). |
| Tag | `span.tag` | Static descriptor in a panel heading. |
| Panel | `section.panel[aria-labelledby]` > `.panel-heading` (h2, then tag/badge/action) > `.scope` > body | One h2 per panel. A panel is a grid spaced by `gap` (16 px); components carry no outer margin; a heading's description sits 8 px under it. No dimming, no hover. |
| Subpanel | `.subpanel` | Top rule and a 12 px grid rhythm for a section inside a panel or card (`.workflows`, `.candidate-review`). |
| Tray | `.tray` | A raised group of related settings inside a panel (the workflow run settings). |
| Meta line | `.meta` | A muted evidence sentence (run detail, plan meta, worktree, usage, diff meta); its `code` identities stay at full contrast, figures are tabular. |
| Button | `button` (secondary), `.primary`, `.danger`, `.text-button` | One `.primary` per action group. `.danger` and `.text-button` are small. Disabled uses the disabled colour tokens, never opacity. |
| Field | `label` wrapping `input`/`textarea` | Label text above the field. `spellCheck={false}` fields render monospace. A checkbox label is an inline row. |
| Field row | `.field-row` | Side-by-side fields that share the row and wrap one per line below 2 × 14 rem; a trailing `small` takes the full row. |
| Form footer | `.form-footer` > `small` + primary | Hint left, primary right even when it wraps. |
| Form group | `.form-group` | A bordered, unfilled group around a form (register, ticket). |
| Action row | `.actions` | Wrapping row; a trailing `small` takes the full row; `.danger` goes to the end. |
| Facts | `dl.facts` > `div` > `dt` + `dd` | Full identities in `dd code`. Term column 150 px, one column at 680 px (at 920 px inside a candidate, where every value is a full hash). |
| Record list | `ul.record-list` > `li.record` | Bordered rows: baselines, recipes, tickets, checks, findings. A nested record alternates its surface. `data-tone` on a leaf record (baseline, check, finding) adds a toned rule on its leading edge; a ticket card carries its state in its run badge, not a page-length rule. `.record-headed` puts the title and badge on the first line and every later child on its own full-width line. |
| Selectable card | `button.run-card[aria-pressed]` > `.run-prompt` + `.run-meta` | Selection shows by fill, border and a lavender inset rule, not colour alone. `.run-prompt` may clamp prose to two lines, never identities. |
| Reason and next step | `.failure-note[data-tone]` then `.recovery-note` | The reason carries an 8 px-inset rule and text in the tone of the state it explains; the next step follows flush under it, ruled in lavender, whether nested in the reason or its next sibling. |
| Callout | `.callout[data-tone]` | Toned box for outages, open questions and the runtime's activity status. |
| Alert banner | `.error[role=alert]` with a Dismiss `.text-button` | Refused actions and failed loads only; always dismissible. Outages are `role=status`, not alerts. |
| Disclosure | `details` > `summary`; `details.section` for a section heading (diff, check evidence, event record) | CSS caret, never text, so it adds nothing to the accessible name; the caret aligns with the content edge. |
| Scroll region | `ol.events`, `pre[aria-label][tabIndex=0]` | The only elements that scroll; bounded by `--scroll-max` (`--plan-max` for the plan). Focusable, with an inset focus ring. |
| Empty state | `.empty` (inline text), `.empty-box` (dashed box), `.activity-empty` | Muted text; the glyph is `aria-hidden`. |

## Screens

- **App shell** (`App.tsx`, `screens/app.css`): skip link, topbar (wordmark, stage, connection status with a tone mark), intro, the runtime connection panel, Projects, then the workspace of session history and the main column (start form, session events). The workspace is two columns above 920 px and one column at 920 px and below, in DOM order, matching the Projects rail.
- **Projects** (`Projects.tsx`, `screens/projects.css`): a rail with the register form and project cards, and a detail column: facts first (the first `.facts` on the page), the "Rebind repository" disclosure, the action row (a running baseline adds its `.danger` cancel), baselines (each with its reason and next step and a log button per recipe stream, then the opened log), discovery (questions callout, problems, recipes, the manifest form), the Workflows subpanel, then the project event record.
- **Workflows** (`Workflows.tsx`, `screens/workflows.css`): the ticket form (each field followed by its UTF-8 byte count), the run settings (paths, writes, approver, plan budgets, provider and model, automatic repair), then ticket cards. A ticket card holds its head, intent, actions with the run badge (the first writer's `.danger` cancel sits before the badge; a held-back "Plan r{n+1}" names its reason on its own line), the confirmation checkbox when the next revision would leave a pending, approved or reviewed revision behind, the writer's activity callout, the plan review with the complete plan in a bounded region, plan meta, earlier revisions with their badges, the reason and next step, worktree lines and the candidate.
- **Candidate review** (`CandidateReview.tsx`, `screens/candidate-review.css`): heading with badge, full identities, the action row, the runtime's activity callout, reason and next step, the diff, check evidence with logs, the independent review with findings, and usage.

## Accessibility

- Every visible text run meets 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) against its painted background in both schemes; marks, control edges and focus meet 3:1. Disabled controls are exempt and are marked with the `disabled` attribute.
- The first Tab stop is "Skip to main content", which focuses `main#main`. Focus is always visible.
- Every field has a label; every control has a name; scroll regions are focusable; heading levels never skip; every alert has a Dismiss button; `html[lang=en]`.
- No horizontal page scroll at the Tauri window's 760 px minimum width. Containers that can hold code use `min-width: 0` and `minmax(0, 1fr)`.
- Reduced motion turns the one transition off. Forced colours keep marks and selection visible.

## Enforcement

`npm test` runs `design/design-system.test.ts`. It reads stylesheets with `node:fs`, because Vitest replaces `*.css?raw` imports with an empty string, and it fails on an empty sheet so no check can pass vacuously. It asserts:

- Outside `tokens.css`: no colour literal or function, no raw length or duration, font sizes only from `--text-*`, no `opacity`, no `!important`, approved media queries only, `outline: none` only on `main:focus`, scrolling only on labelled scroll regions, no truncation of `code`/`pre`, tone mapping only in `components.css`, no selector named after a runtime state, tone variables read only by a rule whose selector carries `[data-tone]`, and screen selectors scoped by a unique class with at most three child steps.
- Every `var()` resolves; both schemes define the same colour roles; every semantic pair meets its WCAG ratio in both schemes.
- Every component file is registered, and each screen keeps its heading levels, has no inline styles or positive `tabIndex`, renders badges through `StatusBadge`, and every alert carries Dismiss.
- The tone taxonomy: exactly the five evidence states are success; interruption is never danger; the badge renders the runtime text unchanged.

`node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` checks the rendered result: contrast of every visible text run against its composited background in both schemes, that the client follows the system scheme, no horizontal scroll at 760 px, plus the existing keyboard, accessibility, DOM and lifecycle checks.

## Changing the system

A new colour is a token in both schemes plus a contrast pair in the test. A new runtime state is a tone in `tone.ts`. A new component goes in `components.css` and this table. Do not style by runtime state name, add a heading level, or move the DOM elements the smoke reads (listed in `scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs`). Run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` (Node 24.19.0) and the desktop smoke, and report each result.


---

Source: /docs/docs-implementation-roadmap

# Implementation roadmap and AI handoff

Date: 2026-10-16. This is the implementation sequence from the audited foundation to a usable MVP and full v1. It supplements [the current architecture](CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md), not a claim that the planned capabilities already exist.

## Starting point

Keep the application and all three maintained CLI components in **this monorepo**. Missions, Atlas, and Beacon retain independent package/API boundaries, compatible data formats, and upstream MIT notices. Repository separation is a later maintenance decision, not a prerequisite or the next assignment. Do not create repositories, remove component source, or replace these tools with Rust rewrites to advance a milestone.

[FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md) records the observed evidence. Its current Linux baseline is 101 Rust tests, 18 API-client tests, 4 scope-guard tests, 20 positive/negative schema checks, and 3,092 component tests passing, with Rust formatting/lint and frontend type/build checks passing, plus an 18-check synthetic smoke-harness run, the 19-check genuine OpenRouter run, the 15-check M2a browser smoke, a genuine passing baseline of this checkout, the 8-check M2b browser smoke and the genuine M2c writer runs recorded in the status report. Counts describe that audit, not a permanent expected total; future changes must rerun appropriate checks.

| Area | Implemented and checked | Partial or not yet demonstrated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repository | MIT/notices, cleaned current tracking, contributor rules, pinned tools/locks, CI definitions | Historical session files remain in earlier commits; remote CI and distribution need separate evidence |
| Domain/storage | Immutable plan hashing, exact approval/revision/project guards, candidate/review guards, transactional state/events, durable SQLite runs, restart interruption | A real baseline executor is absent; storage deliberately rejects entry to feature implementation |
| Pi/runtime | Actual Pi 1.3.0 version/RPC handshake, authenticated loopback run API, replay/SSE, timeout/cancel/reap, malformed/error fixtures, durable failed/cancelled attempts | Genuine provider-backed output observed on Linux on October 17, 2026 (OpenRouter `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, 19/19 real-mode smoke checks); Mac/Windows service lifecycle and native client remain unverified |
| Frontend | Typed client, real service connection, run/history/cancel/reconnect, private in-memory token; browser smoke exercised | Tauri shell exists; native GUI launch, installer, and Mac/Windows results are unverified |
| Maintained CLIs | Independent public Missions, Atlas, Beacon repositories with passing standalone CI, compatible legacy aliases and exact-commit submodule consumption (ADR 0012) | Runtime ticket/knowledge/prompt adapters are not integrated; packages remain private/unpublished |
| Product workflow | Foundational contracts and negative tests; M2a read-only import, discovery proposals and confirmed manifest revisions with replay; M2b supervised baseline execution with commit/tree/environment-bound evidence and the transactional implementation gate; M2c temporary tickets, immutable plans, exact-hash approvals, Luuna-owned worktree leases and one scoped writer (October 17, 2026) | Candidate validation and independent review (M3), multi-repo scheduling, Missions/Atlas/Beacon adapters, publication, TUI parity and release installation remain planned |

M0 is substantially established, with remaining API/capability/threat-model details completed alongside their first executable consumers. It is not proof of the operational workflow. M1 is closed on Linux as of October 17, 2026; its native-host step is carried by the MVP native-lifecycle item. M2a, M2b and M2c closed later the same day (see the status report). M3 and the MVP gate closed on Linux and Windows, and the M4–M8 slices recorded under each milestone below landed on October 21, 2026 with the gaps each status names; the next assignments are evidence on hosts this one is not (Mac, capable mobile runners, a clean machine, real GitHub), never a shortcut around them.

## What counts as a usable product

A **usable single-repository MVP** imports a real repository, discovers and confirms a meaningful baseline, prepares an exact plan, gets human approval, implements a bounded change in a Luuna-owned worktree, runs real required checks, obtains fresh independent review, and preserves evidence through cancellation or restart. The desktop must show the actual state and allow recovery. It must be demonstrated on the chosen Mac/Windows targets before those targets are advertised.

The MVP can deliver reviewable local commits/diffs without automatic PRs, multi-repository orchestration, all stack profiles, complete memory integration, or a TUI. Those omissions must be explicit.

**Full v1** additionally satisfies all R01–R15 and the [acceptance matrix](11-acceptance.md): multi-repository roles and integration, project creation and supported profiles, scoped memory and component adapters, browser/TUI parity, linked automatic PRs, human-only merging, and supported fresh-host installation. Optional remote workers, NAS hosting, GPU inference, semantic retrieval, team/SaaS features, and a full IDE are later work.

## Milestones and measurable exits

Follow the existing M0–M8 naming. Desktop work accompanies real runtime slices rather than becoming a separate simulated product.

### M1 — Finish genuine engine compatibility

**Depends on:** existing foundation, a supported model/provider, private credentials, and usable provider network access.

1. Inspect the installed pinned Pi protocol docs and current adapter. Reuse the credential-free probe and synthetic fixtures.
2. Complete one small genuine provider-backed request through the authenticated local API. Observe actual text/event streaming and the correct `agent_settled` completion semantics.
3. Cancel another genuine in-flight request and show that the owned process exits/reaps and the final state is cancelled. Exercise provider failure/timeout without promoting partial output to success.
4. Disconnect/reconnect the client and stop/restart the service. Replay ordered persisted events, retain completed/failed/cancelled history, and mark an abandoned active attempt interrupted.
5. Run the native desktop against the same service on a capable host; record any platform gap rather than calling a web build a native launch.

**Exit:** sanitized provider/Pi/model/platform evidence, real output, cancellation/error traces, persistent run IDs/cursors, and unchanged privacy/authentication protections. Missing-key failure already has evidence; it does not substitute for model success. Tool-free success closes connectivity, not repository-writing readiness. Map to R03/R15.

### M2a — Import and read-only discovery

**Depends on:** M1's stable lifecycle and event contract. Read-only fixture/API work can proceed while provider access is being configured.

Register an existing single repository, establish stable identity/remote/base commit, detect dirty state, discover candidate stack/check recipes, and ask the developer to confirm uncertain repository facts. Persist project/manifest revisions and expose them through authenticated API/client contracts. Use canonical `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets` when ticket creation is introduced.

**Exit:** a real and a synthetic repository import without changing their contents; dirty files remain byte-identical; an invalid or mismatched repository is rejected; replay reconstructs the confirmed map. Discovery proposes commands rather than silently executing arbitrary repository text. This begins R04 and supplies M2 inputs.

**Status (October 17, 2026): closed on Linux.** `luuna-git`, `luuna-discovery`, the project registry in `luuna-storage`, the five project routes, the client and the desktop panel exist with synthetic and real (this checkout) evidence; see [ADR 0006](decisions/0006-repository-import.md) and the status report. Relationships between repositories are accepted by the contract but not discovered; that is M4.

### M2b — Baseline and check evidence

**Depends on:** confirmed repository identity and check recipes from M2a.

Build a supervised command executor with executable/argument arrays, explicit cwd/profile, timeouts, capability checks, private artifacts, and process ownership. Record command, environment, exact commit/tree, timestamps, exit/status, and artifact hashes. Establish required baseline evidence before feature writes. Missing testing setup creates a bounded prerequisite workflow requiring its own approval.

**Exit:** genuine passing and deliberately failing fixture baselines; missing executable, empty/missing test setup, cancelled command, and incapable host remain blocked/failed/interrupted as appropriate. A baseline from another commit/environment cannot unlock a writer. Retain the fail-closed storage guard until this evidence is checked transactionally. Map to R08 and support R13.

**Status (October 17, 2026): closed on Linux.** `luuna-executor`, baseline contracts, storage migration 3 with `begin_implementation`, the baseline routes, client and desktop controls exist; this checkout's own `cargo test --locked --workspace` and `npm test` baseline passed with bound evidence, and the failure, blocked, cancelled and interrupted paths are tested; see [ADR 0007](decisions/0007-baseline-executor.md) and the status report. A dirty checkout is blocked until M2c worktrees exist.

### M2c — Exact approval and one scoped writer

**Depends on:** M2b; existing plan/approval domain and SQLite guards.

Expose immutable plan revisions and exact-hash approvals through runtime/API/client. Revalidate ticket/manifest/base revision and baseline evidence when scheduling. Create only Luuna-owned branches/worktrees with durable ownership/leases. Execute one bounded writer assignment with declared resources, operation scope, budgets, and model profile. Separate native-host permissions from any advertised isolation mechanism.

**Exit:** one approved fixture feature changes only its managed worktree; the developer checkout is preserved. Missing/stale approval, changed base, changed recipe, unrelated repository/path, stale baseline, second writer, and exceeded budget are rejected. Cancellation/restart preserves unfinished work and invalidates uncertain evidence. Map to R07/R08. A prompt that promises to obey paths is not an OS security boundary.

**Status (October 17, 2026): closed on Linux.** Temporary local tickets (ADR 0003/0005), runtime-built immutable plan revisions, exact-hash approvals, `begin_implementation` revalidation of ticket, manifest, base, baseline and host fingerprint, worktree leases with one active lease per repository, attempts counted against the budget, the Pi writer profile with the Luuna scope guard, post-session scope judgement of the worktree diff and candidate commits exist; every exit rejection, cancellation and restart is tested, and a genuine pinned-Pi writer through a real provider is recorded in the status report; see [ADR 0008](decisions/0008-approval-worktrees-writer.md). The Missions adapter replaces the temporary ticket in M6; baselines still run on the developer checkout, so a dirty checkout still blocks a baseline.

### M3 — Candidate checks, independent review, repair and recovery

**Depends on:** a real M2 writer and command evidence.

Freeze exact candidate commit/tree identities; bind required checks and structured reviewer results to them. Start the reviewer in a new session with requirements, current code/diff, and evidence, excluding the implementer's conversation. Classify infrastructure failures separately, aggregate attempt/time/cost usage, bound repairs, and pause usefully when exhausted. Every repair/manual edit invalidates affected evidence and review.

**Exit:** a seeded regression is blocked; a stale candidate/review cannot pass; repair exhaustion persists with artifacts; restart does not reset budgets or duplicate work; cancellation covers owned descendants when shell tools are enabled. Demonstrate a complete approved single-repo feature with real checks and independent review. Map to R09/R10.

**Implementation status (October 17, 2026):** candidate command checks, fresh read-only Pi reviewer sessions, structured review bindings, bounded manual/opt-in automatic repair, aggregate budgets, restart recovery and desktop diff/evidence views are implemented and fixture-tested. **The genuine-provider exit is closed on Linux** by `scripts/m3-smoke.mjs` through OpenRouter with pinned Pi 1.3.0: real writer, real required checks, fresh independent reviewer, seeded failure → repair r2 → fresh evidence, bounded automatic repair pausing at the attempt budget, cancellation and hard-kill recovery with spend reservation. A real run on the MVP code (`fd42d59`, October 21, 2026) passed 61/61 again. Native Mac/Windows proof remains open, so M3 is not declared fully closed. See [ADR 0009](decisions/0009-candidate-validation-review.md) and the status report.

### MVP gate — Make the single-repository workflow usable

**Depends on:** M1–M3. Develop screens against those working APIs, not alternative frontend state machines.

Complete project import, baseline, plan approval, live execution, diff/evidence/review, history, cancel and recovery flows. Test keyboard access and clear blocked/failure messages. Exercise desktop-to-service reconnection and explicit service shutdown. Smoke native Mac/Windows hosts with declared prerequisites; test backup/migration recovery and document manual service startup limitations.

**Exit:** another developer follows the documented setup and completes the representative fixture workflow without undocumented database edits or fake data. Publish a requirement/evidence report naming MVP omissions. A native package may be a development distribution; signed fresh-host installation remains M7 evidence.

**Status (October 21, 2026): the cloud-doable part is closed on Linux; the native-host part remains.** A candidate whose required checks passed but whose reviewer left no verdict can be re-validated in place as a fresh generation of the same revision under the same approval and budgets (ADR 0009, point 7). An orderly shutdown now records interruption, never cancellation (ADR 0004 note). The desktop client shows outages, reconnects and reloads by itself, names the next allowed action with every refusal and recorded reason, and is operable by keyboard; `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` drives it through the documented [walkthrough](MVP-WALKTHROUGH.md) with recovery, refusal, keyboard and accessibility checks, and [MVP-EVIDENCE.md](MVP-EVIDENCE.md) is the requirement/evidence report naming the omissions. **Later on October 21, 2026, on Windows:** the backup/migration recovery drill is scripted (`node scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs`, 31/31 on this host, walkthrough step 7b) and the Windows native smoke is covered by the PR 11 bundled-WebView2 lifecycle run plus `scripts/package-windows.ps1`; the Mac smoke remains open for lack of a host.

### M4 — Multi-repository coordination

**Depends on:** M3's reliable single-repository execution and candidate guards.

Add confirmed repository relationships, task DAG scheduling, scoped project/repository/specialist roles, leases, bounded concurrency, dependency overrides, and cross-repository candidate sets. Preserve one authoritative runtime.

**Exit:** an API/shared-package/consumer fixture produces three exact candidate commits, independent work runs within limits, incompatible consumer integration blocks completion, and partial failure/restart preserves the graph and evidence. Map to R05/R06; single-repository check success cannot stand in for integration success.

**Status (October 21, 2026): closed with the synthetic writer on Windows.** Validated task graphs, relationship proposals and confirmation, durable per-task state, the dependency-ordered scheduler with `max_workers`, cross-repository candidate sets with bindings, per-repository validation with a combined review diff, integration blocking, and resumption by task exist and are tested by the three-repository fixture (`crates/luuna-runtime/tests/multirepo.rs`, 9 scenarios); see [ADR 0017](decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md) and the status report. Open: delegated roles (P42), dependency overrides (P44), repair of a multi-repository set (re-planning by decision) and a genuine-provider multi-repository feature.

### M5 — New projects and verified stack profiles

**Depends on:** M2's executor/baseline contracts; end-to-end acceptance uses M3/M4 as appropriate.

Add approved scaffolding and check profiles for React/Next.js/TypeScript, Node, Go, Python, Flutter, native Android and iOS. Probe host capabilities; let the developer confirm discovered recipes.

**Exit:** every advertised profile has a genuine scaffold/import baseline on a capable runner. Required Apple/device/emulator checks have real evidence or explicitly block that workflow. Do not call an unavailable platform passing. Map to R04/R13.

**Status (October 21, 2026): implemented; closed only for the profiles this Windows host can run.** Host capability probing, capability-annotated discovery for every advertised profile, and hashed, confirmed scaffolding with a real baseline exist ([ADR 0019](decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md)); Node, TypeScript, Python and Rust scaffolds ran passing baselines here, Go, Flutter, Android and iOS are proved only as correctly blocked proposals and annotated discoveries. Capable-runner evidence for those four and the Mac-only checks remain the exit.

### M6 — Integrated components, scoped memory and client parity

**Depends on:** stable project/ticket/run contracts; client parity acceptance depends on the implemented product capabilities.

Integrate Missions tickets/dependencies with serialized revision checks; migrate any temporary SQLite ticket authority into a reconciled projection. Add Atlas user/project/process memory with provenance, isolation, promotion/deletion and lexical retrieval. Render versioned Beacon prompts into explicit Pi resources. Use compatible APIs/data formats rather than independent writable copies or imported historical task records.

Complete browser and TUI actions against a shared capability catalog, alongside the desktop. Include plans, approval, repository views, diff/review, settings, memory, cancel, recovery and publication controls.

**Exit:** external Missions edits cause a detected conflict; stale prompts/schema mismatches fail visibly; private memory never crosses project/export scope; every cataloged action and failure path has parity evidence; reconnect yields the same authoritative state. Map to R02/R14/R15.

**Status (October 21, 2026): closed for the cataloged actions on Windows and Linux.** Missions migration and reconciliation and selected Atlas/Beacon context (ADR 0014), memory promotion and the scope-safe export (ADR 0021), the capability catalog, shared failure explanations and the terminal client with parity tests and `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs` (ADR 0020) exist; see the status report. Open: a keyboard audit and tones for the interactive TUI, import of an export, memory retention policy.

### M7 — Publication and portable installation

**Depends on:** M3 evidence gates, M4 candidate sets, and a verified publication credential mechanism.

Implement push/linked PR creation, durable idempotency and remote reconciliation, partial-success recovery, CI observation and human-controlled merge tracking. Ship tested installers/doctor diagnostics and a host-specific independent-service/token/update strategy. Current permission to push this repository is not proof the future product publisher exists.

**Exit:** approved three-repo candidates create linked PRs once, timeout-after-success and partial publication recover without duplicates, failing CI is distinct from integration, and no automatic merge path exists. Clean supported Mac/Windows computers install, configure and run the fixture without NAS/cloud dependence. Map to R01/R11/R12.

**Status (October 21, 2026): implemented against a fake GitHub API and a local remote; installer built unsigned on Windows.** Publication with a durable intent ledger, reconciliation, CI and merge observation and no merge path, plus `luuna-runtime doctor`, exist and pass six scenarios ([ADR 0018](decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md)); `scripts/package-windows.ps1` produces an NSIS development installer carrying the runtime, helper scripts and the pinned Pi tree. Open: real GitHub evidence, a clean-machine Windows installation, Mac packaging, signing.

### M8 — Full-v1 release evidence

**Depends on:** M4–M7 and every advertised capability's prerequisites.

Run all A01–A34 scenarios, supported-host/version matrix, real-project pilot, failure/recovery drills, migrations/backups, dependency/security review and performance measurements. Inspect resource growth, cancellation latency, event delivery and usage accounting; define targets from observed measurements.

**Exit:** every R01–R15 requirement has passing linked evidence on relevant hosts; unresolved required checks block the v1 label. Document limitations, credential/retention boundaries, installer provenance and reproducible recovery. No required path depends on synthetic model output.

**Status (October 21, 2026): report produced; the v1 label is not granted.** [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) links every requirement and scenario to the evidence that exists, `node scripts/release-evidence.mjs` runs the checks and harnesses into one requirement-mapped report, and the blocking items (Mac, clean-machine installation, real GitHub, capable runners for Flutter/Android/iOS, a genuine run on the current tree, a real-project pilot) are named there.

## Requirement coverage

| Requirement | Delivery/evidence ownership |
| --- | --- |
| R01 Local Mac/Windows operation | MVP native smoke, M7 fresh-host installs, M8 release matrix |
| R02 Browser/TUI capability parity | M6 catalog and parity suite, M8 |
| R03 Pi with selected models | M1 genuine engine/model compatibility, repeated after upgrades |
| R04 Import and creation | M2a import; M5 approved project scaffolding |
| R05 Multiple repositories | M4 confirmed graph and integration candidate |
| R06 Scoped coordination roles | M4 scheduler/assignment traces |
| R07 Approval before feature writes | M2c runtime negative cases, maintained through M8 |
| R08 Meaningful passing baseline | M2b prerequisite/baseline evidence |
| R09 Real checks and fresh review | M3 candidate-bound command/reviewer results |
| R10 Bounded repair and useful pause | M3 aggregate budgets and recovery drills |
| R11 Automatic linked PRs | M7 actual remote publication/reconciliation |
| R12 Developer controls merging | M7/M8 no automatic merge operation |
| R13 Supported stack profiles | M5 capable-host matrix; unavailable required checks block |
| R14 Scoped memory | M6 privacy/provenance/deletion tests |
| R15 Runtime outlives clients | M1 reconnect/restart, MVP native lifecycle, M7 packaged service |

## Implementation process and evidence

Make each M2 substage and each subsequent bounded behavior independently reviewable. Before coding, inspect current code, applicable instructions, relevant schema/API/role contract, and baseline evidence. Describe the behavior, affected files/boundaries, negative cases, and exit command; do not ask the user to repeat accepted architecture decisions.

Implement runtime policy and durable transitions before connecting client actions. Use synthetic fixtures for deterministic failure cases and real tools/providers for compatibility evidence. Run relevant checks, get independent review, fix material findings, and update status and handoff before advancing. Add crates/packages when a real implementation needs them. Consume the independent component repositories through the exact-commit submodules of ADR 0012.

Each completion report must identify:

- Revision and dirty-state context; delivered behavior and requirement IDs.
- Commands actually run, exit results, counts, OS/architecture and pinned tool/provider/model versions.
- Run/attempt IDs, event cursors, exact plan/candidate hashes, and sanitized artifact locations.
- Negative/failure/recovery cases exercised; independent reviewer findings and resolution.
- Passing, failing, blocked and unavailable checks separately, with the next concrete assignment.

Commit only sanitized summaries, synthetic fixtures and useful reproducible tests. Keep tokens, keys, personal paths, private provider transcripts and raw local state out of Git. Record private evidence references without copying secrets. A documentation report cannot replace missing execution evidence.

## Reproducible starting commands

Pins: Rust **1.90.0**, Node **24.19.0**, npm **11.9.0**, Bun **1.4.3**, Pi **1.3.0**. Root and native Cargo workspaces have separate locks; root npm, Pi and each Bun component also have their own committed locks.

For the configured cloud checkout, `bash scripts/setup-cloud.sh` installs frozen dependencies and builds the runtime without component lifecycle hooks. Use the saved environment startup instructions for tool/cache paths. On other hosts follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and platform prerequisites rather than assuming `/workspace` exists.

From the repository root:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked --workspace
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run build
node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs
git diff --check
```

For a changed component, run in its own directory:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run verify
```

Run the native check on a capable host; root Rust checks exclude that workspace:

```sh
cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
```

With `LUUNA_PI_COMMAND` pointing to the installed pinned executable:

```sh
cargo run --locked -p luuna-engine-pi --example probe
```

That probe makes **no model request**. For genuine M1 proof, securely set the provider credential (or its `LUUNA_PI_<NAME>` alias) in the runtime environment, build the runtime, and run `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider <provider> --model <model>`, which starts the runtime itself and writes a sanitized report; or start `cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime` manually with `LUUNA_API_TOKEN`, provider and model set. Launch `npm run dev` or `npm run desktop` separately. The runtime does not automatically load `.env`. See the [runtime README](../crates/luuna-runtime/README.md), [desktop README](../apps/desktop/README.md), and [Pi fixtures](../fixtures/pi-rpc/README.md).

## Planning ranges, assumptions and critical path

These are engineering estimates from this foundation, **not promised dates**. Assume one experienced full-time engineer using AI assistance, about 40 scheduled hours/week with **30 focused engineering hours**, a stable model/provider budget, Mac and Windows capable hosts, and timely feedback. AI assistance is included in the assumption; it does not remove integration, review, native packaging, or failure-testing work. Waiting for credentials, network changes, host access, signing, or external service approval adds elapsed time.

The earlier desktop proposal estimated **372–600 hours from scratch** for a meaningful single-repository MVP. Some bootstrap work now exists and its model path was proved on October 17, 2026; its native paths remain unproven. Use the following remaining-work range provisionally and re-estimate after the first real M2 writer.

| Remaining work to a usable single-repo MVP | Focused hours before contingency |
| --- | ---: |
| Genuine M1 compatibility and evidence (Linux closed October 17, 2026; native-host step remains) | 0–8 |
| M2c approval revalidation, worktree ownership and scoped writer (closed on Linux October 17, 2026; native-host proof remains) | 0–8 |
| M3 independent review, repair and recovery | 64–104 |
| MVP client completion, native smoke and end-to-end hardening | 64–104 |
| Subtotal | 128–224 |
| Technical uncertainty allowance, approximately 20% | 26–45 |
| **Planning range** | **154–269** |

That is about **4–7 full 40-hour engineering weeks**, or **5–9 elapsed workweeks at 30 focused hours/week** under these assumptions. A connectivity preview can arrive sooner; it is not the usable MVP defined above.

| Additional work after the MVP to full v1 | Focused hours before contingency |
| --- | ---: |
| M4 multi-repository scheduler and integration | 96–160 |
| M5 creation and complete stack-profile matrix | 128–224 |
| M6 component/memory integration and browser/TUI parity | 128–224 |
| M7 linked publication, service packaging and installers | 96–168 |
| M8 pilot, acceptance, security/recovery and release hardening | 80–144 |
| Subtotal | 528–920 |
| Technical uncertainty allowance, approximately 20% | 106–184 |
| **Additional planning range** | **640–1,110** |

The combined remaining full-v1 range is roughly **790–1,380 focused hours**, about **20–35 full engineering weeks** or **26–46 elapsed workweeks at the assumed focused capacity**. Treat the upper range seriously: native/mobile profiles, TUI parity, independent service installation and publication recovery are substantial product work. Requirements changes or missing platforms can exceed this range.

The execution critical path is **genuine M1 → import/baseline → exact approval/scoped writer → candidate checks/fresh review → reliable multi-repo integration**. Full-v1 release also depends on client parity, profile/platform proof and publication/installers. Stack/client contracts can be prepared alongside core work once stable, but one engineer's parallel tasks do not create extra capacity. Re-estimate from measured milestone throughput and preserve required gates; if time is short, narrow the MVP scope explicitly rather than declaring full v1 early.


---

Source: /docs/docs-mvp-walkthrough

# MVP walkthrough: one repository from import to a reviewed candidate

Date: 2026-10-21. This is the representative single-repository workflow another developer follows end to end with the browser client, without editing the database or inventing data. `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` automates exactly these steps against the synthetic Pi fixture and records the result; a real provider follows the same steps with real model output. Read [AI-START-HERE.md](../AI-START-HERE.md) for the pins and [CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md](CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md) for what each step may and may not claim.

What the walkthrough does not cover is listed in [MVP-EVIDENCE.md](MVP-EVIDENCE.md): no publication or merge, one repository, no TUI, no memory integration, and no native Mac/Windows proof.

## 0. Prerequisites

- Rust 1.90.0, Node 24.19.0 with npm 11.9.0, Python 3, Git, and the pinned Pi 1.3.0 installed from `tools/pi` (`bash scripts/setup-cloud.sh` on the cloud image; [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) elsewhere). `npm ci --ignore-scripts` at the root.
- A provider credential for a real run, exported as `LUUNA_PI_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` (for example `LUUNA_PI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) in the shell that starts the runtime. Never type it into the client. Without a credential, rehearse with the synthetic fixture as described in [the credential-free rehearsal](#credential-free-rehearsal-with-the-synthetic-fixture); its runs are protocol evidence only.
- A repository to import with a test command that can pass on this host. The fixture used below is a small Python package with `python -m unittest -v`.

### Credential-free rehearsal with the synthetic fixture

`fixtures/pi-rpc/mock_pi.py` stands in for Pi. It is not a model: it acts only on `fixture:<name>` markers in the ticket's acceptance criteria, and its writer only ever rewrites `src/main.py` (to print one line). Without a marker the writer changes nothing and the workflow fails with "writer settled without changing any file". Start the runtime of step 1 with these settings instead of a provider:

```sh
export LUUNA_PI_COMMAND=python3
export LUUNA_PI_ARGS_JSON="[\"$PWD/fixtures/pi-rpc/mock_pi.py\"]"   # run from the Luuna checkout
export LUUNA_PI_PROVIDER=test LUUNA_PI_MODEL=synthetic
```

Import a repository whose tests still pass after that rewrite, for example:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/luuna-rehearsal/src && cd /tmp/luuna-rehearsal
git init -q -b main && git remote add origin https://example.invalid/rehearsal.git
printf '__pycache__/\n' > .gitignore
printf '[project]\nname = "rehearsal"\n' > pyproject.toml
printf "print('fixture')\n" > src/main.py
cat > test_main.py <<'PY'
import subprocess, sys, unittest

class MainTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_main_prints(self):
        completed = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "src/main.py"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        self.assertTrue(completed.stdout.strip())
PY
git add -A && git commit -qm "rehearsal fixture"
```

Then follow the steps below with the manifest check `python3 -m unittest -v` (`required: true`), keep `src` in the writer paths, and put a marker on its own line in the acceptance criteria. The first `fixture:` marker selects the writer; the reviewer answers the first `fixture:review_*` marker and passes otherwise:

- `fixture:write_in_scope`: the writer rewrites `src/main.py` and the review passes, so the candidate reaches `reviewed`.
- `fixture:review_malformed_once`: the writer does the same, the first review is malformed and the next one passes, which rehearses re-validation (step 6).
- `fixture:review_blocking`: the review returns `changes_required` with a blocking finding, which rehearses repair.
- `fixture:review_hold`: the reviewer waits 60 s, long enough to cancel or stop the runtime mid-review (step 7).
- `fixture:slow`: the writer waits 60 s, long enough to cancel it from the ticket (step 5).
- `fixture:no_change` and `fixture:write_out_of_scope`: the writer fails closed with the no-change or scope reason and its next step.

## 1. Start the runtime, then the client

```sh
export LUUNA_API_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"      # private; at least 32 bytes
export LUUNA_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.luuna"                   # SQLite, worktrees and private artifacts
export LUUNA_PI_PROVIDER=openrouter LUUNA_PI_MODEL=openai/gpt-4.1   # or set them per action in the client
cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime                    # listens on http://127.0.0.1:4242
```

In a second shell, `npm run dev` and open `http://127.0.0.1:1420`. Press Tab once: the first stop is "Skip to main content". Enter the runtime URL and the token in the connection form and press Enter. The header reads "Local runtime connected"; the token field disappears and the token is kept only in memory.

If the token is wrong the alert says so and names the next step: check the `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` the service was started with and connect again.

## 2. Import the repository (M2a)

In Projects, enter a name, a repository ID (`app`) and the absolute path of the checkout, then "Register repository". The runtime inspects the checkout read-only (optional locks off, hooks neutralised) and shows the redacted remote, the HEAD commit, the branch and the dirty counts. A path that is not a repository root is refused with the runtime's reason ("Registration refused: …").

"Discover proposed map" proposes check recipes from the repository's manifests with evidence and confidence; nothing is executed. Edit the proposed manifest JSON so `checks` holds the commands the project really runs (for the fixture, `python -m unittest -v`, `required: true`), then "Confirm manifest". The facts line reads "revision 1" with the exact base commit, and the ticket form becomes enabled. A draft the runtime cannot read (a misspelled or missing field, or a quoted `"true"`) is refused with the runtime's reason naming the field. A confirmed proposal is spent: run Discover again for the next revision's draft; a stale draft is refused as a revision conflict with that next step.

If the checkout moved or its remote changed on purpose, open "Rebind repository" under the facts, enter the new root path (or leave it empty to re-inspect the registered one), tick the confirmation and rebind. The runtime re-inspects the checkout read-only and records the old and new identity; plans, baselines and approvals stay bound to exact commits, and a manifest whose remote no longer matches must be confirmed again. Every identity-mismatch refusal names this control as the recovery.

## 3. Establish the baseline (M2b)

"Run baseline" executes the confirmed required recipes on the clean developer checkout through the supervised executor and lists the record: status, manifest revision, exact commit, and each recipe's status and exit code. "View unit stdout" and "View unit stderr" open each recipe's log by record identity. The baseline must be `passed` before any writer can start; a failed, blocked or empty suite blocks feature work, and the record says which recipe and why, with the next step (a missing tool or dependency asks for a dependency-preparation recipe such as `npm ci` before the tests). A dirty checkout is blocked until it is clean. "Cancel baseline" stops a running baseline; a second baseline for the same repository waits until the first settles.
